entity.description: One second factor of a person: the authenticator app (DrpnTfTotp: at most one ACTIVE and one live PENDING row per user; a PENDING row older than 15 minutes is ignored; the secret is read only by the code check), or a passkey (DrpnTfPkey, DAR-BE-270: one row per passkey, never PENDING, its credential in PasskeyCredential). Two-factor is on while any row is ACTIVE.

field.name: factorTypeEnumId
field.description: DrpnTfTotp (authenticator app) or DrpnTfPkey (passkey).

field.name: statusId
field.description: PENDING (set up, not confirmed), ACTIVE or ENDED.

field.name: secret
field.description: The TOTP secret, Base32. Returned once, by begin#TwoFactorSetup; never logged or returned again.

field.name: confirmedDate
field.description: When it was turned on (the app's first right code; a passkey's registration).

field.name: endedReason
field.description: USER_OFF, USER_REMOVED, ADMIN_RESET or REPLACED.

field.name: lastUsedTimeStep
field.description: The 30-second step of the last code accepted; a code is accepted only for a later step (no replay).

field.name: failedCodeCount
field.description: Wrong codes since failedWindowStart.

field.name: failedWindowStart
field.description: Start of the 24-hour window failedCodeCount counts in.

field.name: codesLockedDate
field.description: Set at 20 wrong codes in 24 hours: codes are refused until a password reset or an admin reset.

entity.description: DAR-BE-270. The WebAuthn credential behind a DrpnTfPkey TwoFactorFactor row (same factorId). Only a credential whose factor is ACTIVE is used. Not encrypted: a public key and a credential id are not secrets. The row stays after its factor ends (which authenticator, named what). Written only by darpan.facade.auth.PasskeySupport.

field.name: credentialId
field.description: Base64url credential id (up to 1023 bytes).

field.name: credentialIdHash
field.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the credential id bytes: the lookup and the one-live-owner check.

field.name: attestedCredentialData
field.description: Base64url attested credential data as the authenticator gave it at registration: AAGUID (the authenticator model, all zeros when withheld), credential id and COSE public key, in webauthn4j's AttestedCredentialDataConverter layout.

field.name: signCount
field.description: The authenticator's signature counter at its last use; a counter that does not move forward is refused (0 on both sides is allowed: synced passkeys report 0).

field.name: transports
field.description: Comma list the browser reported: internal, hybrid, usb, nfc, ble.

field.name: name
field.description: The person's label, e.g. MacBook Touch ID (60 characters at most).

field.name: backupEligible
field.description: Y: a synced passkey (may be copied to other devices).

field.name: backedUp
field.description: Y: backed up at its last use.

entity.description: One single-use recovery code (80 bits, xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx). Stored as a salted SHA-256 hash only.

field.name: codeSalt
field.description: Random per row.

entity.description: The step between a right password and a session, for a person with two-factor on (enter a code) or due and not set up (set up first). The client holds the token in page memory only; only its SHA-256 is stored. Lives 5 minutes, used once, and 5 wrong codes end it.

field.name: tokenHash
field.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the 32-byte random token.

field.name: purposeEnumId
field.description: DrpnScCode (enter a code or use a passkey), DrpnScSetup (set up first), DrpnScProof (a passkey proof for an action) or DrpnScPkAdd (a passkey registration). For the last two the tokenHash is the SHA-256 of webauthnChallenge, so the browser's clientDataJSON names the row.

field.name: webauthnChallenge
field.description: DAR-BE-270. The WebAuthn challenge (base64url, 32 random bytes) a passkey must sign for this row; not a secret (it is useless without the authenticator). Set by begin#PasskeySignIn, begin#PasskeyProof and begin#PasskeyRegistration; any attempt uses it up.

entity.description: Per-role enforcement switch: from requiredFromDate on, a person in this role cannot get a session without two-factor. Empty = optional (every seed row starts empty, so a deploy changes nothing). A date in the future is the grace period: sign-in still works and prompts. Written only by admin.SecurityAdminServices.update#TwoFactorPolicy.

field.name: permissionGroupId
field.description: ADMIN, DARPAN_SUPER_ADMIN, DARPAN_ADMIN (UserGroupMember) or DARPAN_TENANT_ADMIN (in any tenant).

entity.description: Who actually got in: every setup, code check, recovery code use, turn-off, admin reset and lock. The framework's UserLoginHistory marks the password step successful even when the code then fails, so this is the evidence. Create-only, like AdminAuditLog. Never holds a code or the secret.

field.name: eventType
field.description: SETUP_STARTED, SETUP_CONFIRMED, CODE_OK, CODE_FAILED, RECOVERY_USED, CODES_RENEWED, TURNED_OFF, ADMIN_RESET, CODES_LOCKED or LOCK_CLEARED; DAR-BE-270: PASSKEY_ADDED, PASSKEY_OK, PASSKEY_FAILED, PASSKEY_COUNTER_REGRESSED, PASSKEY_RENAMED, PASSKEY_REMOVED or APP_REMOVED.

field.name: byUserId
field.description: Who did it, when not the person themselves (an admin reset).

field.name: sessionsEndedDate
field.description: DAR-BE-264 (review QH1). When every sign-in of the person was last ended by a two-factor change (a factor first turned on, two-factor turned off, an admin reset): TwoFactorSupport.endSessions deletes the login keys and sets this, never earlier than it was. A web session with no live key of the person (a session cookie alone) that started before it is ended at its next request (AuthSessionSupport.enforceWebSignInLifetime); keys need no date, they are deleted. Read from the UserAccount the framework loads on every request.
